sections.content: A Bank Verification Number (BVN) slip is an official printable document used to prove your 11-digit banking identity and show verified biometric demographics returned directly from the central NIBSS database. Whether you are opening a tier-3 corporate bank account, applying for a foreign visa, or verifying your credentials for employment, having a clear, high-resolution BVN slip with a passport photograph is mandatory across Nigeria. To get your verified document immediately, you can generate your official BVN slip online.

sections.content: What Information Appears on an Official BVN Slip?

items: 11-Digit BVN Number: Your unique national banking identifier displayed prominently in high-contrast bold font.
Full Legal Name: First name, middle name, and surname as officially registered on the central NIBSS biometric database.
Date of Birth & Gender: Recorded demographic data matching your civil registry birth record.
Registered Phone Number: Primary mobile contact line registered to your bank profile.
Biometric Passport Photograph: Digital facial capture extracted directly from your original enrolment session.
Cryptographic QR Code: Scannable 2D barcode used by compliance officers and bank managers to instantly verify authenticity.
Digital Timestamp & Reference: Unique verification transaction tracking reference guaranteeing document freshness.

sections.content: Does a Valid BVN Slip Include a Picture?

Yes, official comprehensive verification slips generated from the NIBSS central repository include the facial photograph taken during your biometric enrolment. While basic USSD codes (*565*0#) only output the 11 raw digits on your phone screen without a photo, institutions such as embassies, visa application centres (TLScontact, VFS Global), civil service boards, and fintech compliance departments require the full picture slip to cross-verify identity.

sections.content: What If Your BVN Slip Shows Inaccurate Details?

If your generated BVN slip reveals an error—such as a misspelled surname, inverted names, or an incorrect date of birth—never use graphic editing tools (Photoshop) to alter the document. Tampering with an official financial document constitutes identity fraud. Instead, use the lawful Ufriends IT BVN Modification Portal to submit official corrections backed by your NIN and legal civil documents.
